short: SREBP-1 and SREBP-2 are bHLH-LZ factors made as ER membrane precursors and activated by sterol-regulated proteolysis, so only the cleaved nuclear fragment binds DNA. They are unusual in having dual specificity: a tyrosine replaces the arginine that is otherwise invariant in bHLH basic regions, letting them bind both the palindromic E-box CACGTG and the non-palindromic sterol regulatory element SRE-1, TCACNCCAC. Sites sit in promoters of cholesterol and fatty acid synthesis genes and work with a neighbouring NF-Y CCAAT box or SP1 GC box, which an isolated SRE needs for activity. The pathway controls the LDL receptor, hepatic lipogenesis and the response to statins, and is central to fatty liver disease and insulin resistance.
long:
## The factors

SREBF1 and SREBF2 encode SREBP-1 and SREBP-2, basic helix-loop-helix leucine zipper (bHLH-LZ) factors that are unusual in being synthesized as membrane-anchored precursors in the endoplasmic reticulum. SREBF1 produces two isoforms from alternative first exons, SREBP-1a and SREBP-1c (also called ADD1), which differ in the length of their activation domain. Each precursor has two transmembrane segments and is held in the ER by SCAP; when sterols are low, SCAP escorts it to the Golgi, where sequential cleavage by Site-1 and Site-2 proteases releases the N-terminal bHLH-LZ fragment, which enters the nucleus and dimerizes. Regulation is therefore proteolytic rather than transcriptional at the level of DNA binding, and only the cleaved nuclear form is a transcription factor. SREBP-2 is the principal driver of cholesterol synthesis genes, SREBP-1c of fatty acid synthesis genes, and SREBP-1a is a stronger general activator expressed mainly in proliferating cells and cell lines. Both genes are broadly expressed, with SREBF1 highest in liver and adipose tissue. The atlas assigns 12 motifs to this family (4 JASPAR, 5 HOCOMOCO, 2 CIS-BP, 1 Vierstra archetype) over SREBF1 and SREBF2, with cohesion 0.89 - the lowest in the E-box group - and SREBF1 (MA0595.1) as the representative.

## The motif

SREBP has dual DNA-binding specificity, and this is the single most important fact about the family. It binds the canonical palindromic E-box CACGTG, usually with T/A flanks (ATCACGTGAT), and it also binds a non-palindromic, non-E-box element, the sterol regulatory element SRE-1, written TCACNCCAC. Mutagenesis of the LDL receptor promoter identified the nucleotides that make SRE-1 an active element, and biochemistry then showed the structural cause: in SREBP the arginine that is otherwise invariant in the basic region of every bHLH protein is replaced by a tyrosine, and that single substitution is sufficient to add SRE recognition to E-box recognition. The co-crystal of the SREBP-1a bHLH-LZ bound to an E-box showed this tyrosine in a position where an alternative rotamer can accommodate the asymmetric SRE. This is why the atlas cannot give the family one consensus. Roughly half of the assigned models are SRE-type (aTCACCCCAc, or its reverse complement aTGGgGTGAt), including the Vierstra archetype AC0486:SREBF:bHLH; the rest are E-box-type (ATCACGTGAT, ATCACcTGAT, gTCAgGTGAt). The published SRE consensus TCACNCCAC and the data consensus aTCACCCCAc agree, with the databases simply filling the degenerate position with the commonest base, C. The two motif classes are not variants of each other in any alignment sense, and a scan using one will miss the other.

## Where it acts

SREBP sites are promoter-proximal, typically within a few hundred base pairs of the transcription start site of lipid-metabolism genes, and they rarely work alone. An isolated SRE is a weak element; efficient activation requires a co-regulatory factor bound nearby, most often NF-Y at a CCAAT box or SP1 at a GC box. The synergy is direct - SREBP contacts the Btd domain of SP1 and the NF-Y trimer - and mapping SREBP1 together with NFY and SP1 genome-wide confirmed that the three co-occupy a large fraction of SREBP-bound promoters. The canonical composite arrangements are the LDLR promoter (SRE-1 plus SP1 sites) and the HMGCS1 promoter (SRE plus NF-Y). Because the nuclear form is generated by proteolysis, occupancy is switched by sterol depletion, statin treatment, insulin (for SREBP-1c) or feeding rather than by changes in site availability.

## Biology and disease

SREBP-2 activates essentially the whole cholesterol biosynthetic pathway plus the LDL receptor, which is why statin treatment, by lowering hepatic sterols, raises LDLR expression through this pathway. SREBP-1c activates fatty acid and triglyceride synthesis and is induced by insulin and by LXR agonists. Targeted disruption of Srebf1 in mice causes partial embryonic lethality, and surviving animals show elevated SREBP-2 and increased cholesterol synthesis, an example of cross-compensation within the family. In humans the pathway sits at the centre of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, hypertriglyceridemia and insulin resistance, and SREBP-driven lipogenesis is also co-opted by tumours; reviews describe the physiology as convergent but the pathophysiology as divergent between the two genes.

## Reading a hit

Decide first which motif you matched. An ATCACGTGAT hit is a T/A-flanked canonical E-box and is indistinguishable from USF, MITF/TFE, BHLHE41 or CLOCK-BMAL1 sites; it is weak evidence for SREBP on its own. A TCACNCCAC hit is much more specific, because few other human factors read that asymmetric sequence, and it becomes considerably stronger if an NF-Y CCAAT box or an SP1 GC box lies within about 50 bp in a lipid-gene promoter. SREBF1 and SREBF2 cannot be distinguished from each other by sequence, and the SREBP-1a/1c isoforms share one DNA-binding domain entirely. Several HOCOMOCO models here are ChIP-only, and one grade-C model (tCgCGTGA) is a degenerate half-site that should not be used for scanning.
caveats: This family has two unrelated motif classes and the databases hold both, so check which one you matched. An ATCACGTGAT E-box hit is shared with USF, MITF/TFE, BHLHE41 and CLOCK-BMAL1 and is weak evidence for SREBP. A TCACNCCAC SRE hit is far more specific, but SREBPs bind it weakly on their own and real elements are usually accompanied by NF-Y or SP1 within about 50 bp. SREBF1 and SREBF2 are indistinguishable by sequence, as are the SREBP-1a and -1c isoforms. Cohesion here is only 0.89 because of the two motif classes, several models are ChIP-only, and one grade-C model is a degenerate half-site not suitable for scanning.
